title: Three change-classification helpers duplicate the same key-diff skeleton
description: The three setNodesRaw/setEdgesRaw change classifiers share one verbatim skeleton: length guard -> per-index loop -> `previous === node` bail -> id-equality bail -> build `new Set([...Object.keys(previous), ...Object.keys(node)])` -> for each key, if it is a managed UI field record a `changed` flag via !Object.is(...), else require Object.is(prevValue,nextValue) and bail false otherwise -> finally return `changed`. They diverge only in which fields are 'tracked' vs 'bail': hasOnlyNodeUiFieldChanges treats position as an extra bail and data-ref as a bail; hasOnlyNodePositionChanges treats position as the tracked delta and UI fields as ignorable; hasOnlyEdgeUiFieldChanges drops position/data entirely. This is incidental duplication (~85 LOC) distinct from the already-known SIMP-02 (which targets the mutators' fingerprint/version bookkeeping, not these classifiers). Note this is a marginal cleanup: the per-helper divergence in tracked-vs-bail field roles means a unified helper would need a small config object, so the readability win is modest.
evidence: hasOnlyNodeUiFieldChanges (196-226), hasOnlyNodePositionChanges (228-253) and hasOnlyEdgeUiFieldChanges (255-281) all contain the identical `const keys = new Set([...Object.keys(previous), ...Object.keys(node/edge)]); for (const key of keys) {... if (UI_FIELDS.has(key)) { if(!Object.is(prev[key],next[key])) changed=true; continue } if (!Object.is(prev[key],next[key])) return false }` block; the node variants additionally early-bail on `previous.data !== node.data` and `!positionsEqual(...)`. REACT_FLOW_NODE_UI_FIELDS (178-185) / REACT_FLOW_EDGE_UI_FIELDS (187) parameterize the only set difference.
est_reduction: ~25-35 LOC if unified behind a single classifyFieldChanges(prev,next,{uiFields,extraBail,tracked}) helper
behavior_preservation: A shared classifier driven by the per-call field-role config produces identical boolean results: same length/identity/id guards, same Object.is comparisons, same UI-vs-structural partition; only the extraction site moves. No observable change to setNodesRaw/setEdgesRaw outputs.
